data.text: Note to Regulatory Authorities: This document may contain protected personal data and/or commercially confidential information exempt from public disclosure. Eli Lilly and Company requests consultation regarding release/redaction prior to any public release. In the United States, this document is subject to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Exemption 4 and may not be reproduced or otherwise disseminated without the written approval of Eli Lilly and Company or its subsidiaries.
Prospective approval of protocol deviations to recruitment and enrollment criteria, also known as protocol waivers or exemptions, is not permitted.
G-CSF permitted up to 48 hours prior.

data.text: Patients with documented history of benign ethnic neutropenia or other conditions could be considered with a lower ANC after discussion with and approval from the Lilly CRP/CRS.

data.text: Platelet transfusion permitted up to 72 hours prior.

data.text: Transfusions to increase the patient's hemoglobin level to at least 8 g/dL are permitted; however, study treatment must not begin until 7 days after the transfusion and CBC criteria for eligibility are confirmed within 24 hr of C1D1.

data.text: Consult with the Lilly CRS/CRP for the appropriate length of time prior to the first dose of study treatment on additional therapies not mentioned.
For agents with known AEs occurring beyond the required wait period outlined in the table, this period must be extended until after the time during which the AE is known to occur.

A patient will be considered significantly noncompliant if he or she is judged by the investigator to have intentionally or repeatedly taken more or less than the prescribed amount of medication. The threshold required to maintain status as compliant will be at least 80% unless otherwise specified in Section 3.6.5 of the specifically enrolled addendum.

Investigators are not obligated to actively seek AEs or SAEs in patients once they have discontinued and/or completed the study (the patient summary CRF has been completed). However, if the investigator learns of any SAE, including a death, at any time after a patient has been discharged from the study, and he/she considers the event reasonably possibly related to the study treatment or study participation, the investigator must promptly notify Lilly.

Planned hospitalizations or procedures for preexisting conditions that were recorded in the patient's medical history at the time of enrollment should not be considered SAEs. Hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization without a precipitating clinical AE (for example, for the administration of study treatment or other protocol-required procedure) should not be considered SAEs.
Serious adverse events, including death, caused by disease progression should not be reported unless the investigator deems them to be possibly related to study treatment.
Bioanalytical samples collected to measure study drug concentration will be retained for a maximum of 1 year following the last patient visit for the study.

A legal representative must give informed consent for a child to participate in this study. In addition to informed consent given by the legal representative, the child may be required to give documented assent, if capable.
The ERB/IRB should include or consult with experts who are knowledgeable in pediatric ethical, clinical, and psychosocial issues.

data.text: have either measurable or evaluable disease using standard techniques by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, Version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1) (Eisenhauer et al. 2009).

data.name: Informed consent and authorization
data.text: The patient, or patient's parent/guardian, has given written informed consent (and assent, as applicable) and authorization for release of health/information for research prior to any study-specific procedures being performed (refer to Appendix 2, Study Governance, Regulatory, and Ethical Considerations).

data.name: Performance score requirement
data.text: The patient has a Lansky (<16 years of age; Lansky et al. 1987) or Karnofsky (≥16 years of age; Karnofsky et al. 1948) performance score of at least 50.

data.name: Discontinuation of previous treatments
data.text: Patients must have discontinued all previous treatments for cancer or investigational agents ≥7 days after the last dose or as shown below, and must have recovered from the acute effects to ≤Grade 2 for alopecia and decreased tendon reflex and to ≤Grade 1 for all other effects at the time of enrollment, unless otherwise noted. For agents with known AEs occurring beyond the required wait period outlined in the table, this period must be extended until after the time during which the AE is known to occur. Consult with the Lilly CRS/CRP for the appropriate length of time prior to the first dose of study treatment on additional therapies not mentioned. Previous treatments and required wait periods: Cytotoxic and myelosuppressive chemotherapy: ≥14 days after the last dose of cytotoxic or myelosuppressive chemotherapy (or ≥42 days if prior nitrosourea); Hematopoietic growth factors: ≥14 days after the last dose of a long-acting growth factor (for example, pegfilgrastim) or ≥48 hours for short-acting growth factor; Cellular therapy: ≥42 days after the completion of any type of cellular therapy (eg modified T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, etc.) agent; Interleukins, interferons, and cytokines (other than hematopoietic growth factors): ≥21 days after the completion of interleukins, interferon, or cytokines (other than hematopoietic growth factors); Antibody therapy: ≥21 days after the last infusion of antibody therapy; Radiotherapy: ≥14 days since local palliative radiation therapy (RT) (small port); craniospinal XRT, or 50% or greater pelvic radiation; ≥42 days for other substantial radiation (such as metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy); Radiopharmaceutical therapy (eg, radiolabeled antibody, 131I-MIBG): ≥42 days after systemically administered radiopharmaceutical therapy; Stem cell infusion without TBI: ≥84 days must have elapsed after auto-transplant or stem cell infusion; Corticosteroids: ≥14 days for patients who have received a course of systemic corticosteroids (≥5 days) to modify immune AEs related to prior therapy. Note: Patients who are on chronic replacement dose for endocrine disorders or are on a stable or decreasing dose for indications other than treating the underlying cancer, may still be eligible (consult Lilly CRP/CRS); Live vaccines: ≥28 days after last live vaccine.

data.name: Adequate hematologic and organ function
data.text: The patient has adequate hematologic and organ function ≤1 week (7 days) prior to first dose of study drug.

data.name: Master Protocol Framework Objective
data.text: The main purpose of the CAMPFIRE Master Protocol is to create a framework to seamlessly evaluate the efficacy and safety of each investigational agent or study drug regimen eligible for development in specified populations of pediatric and young adult patients.

data.name: Investigation-Specific Endpoints
data.text: The clinical research objectives and endpoints for specific investigations are detailed in each individual addendum.

intercurrentEvents.name: Discontinuation of study treatment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues investigational study treatment prior to the investigation-specific primary endpoint assessment, for any reason including adverse events, disease progression, withdrawal of consent, or investigator decision

intercurrentEvents.name: Use of prohibited or rescue concomitant therapy
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient initiates prohibited concomitant therapy or rescue medication as defined in the investigation-specific addendum prior to the primary endpoint assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Death prior to primary endpoint assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient dies before the primary efficacy endpoint can be assessed, particularly relevant for non-survival endpoints such as tumor response

intercurrentEvents.name: Transition to continued-access phase
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient transitions to the continued-access phase (Section 7.8.1.1) prior to completion of the primary endpoint assessment period

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient undergoes a dose reduction or dose interruption of the investigational agent as defined in the investigation-specific addendum

data.description: Prior treatment (e.g., modified T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells) requiring washout of ≥42 days after completion before first dose of study treatment.

data.name: Radiotherapy

data.name: Radiopharmaceutical therapy

data.name: Stem cell infusion (without TBI)
data.description: Prior auto-transplant or stem cell infusion requiring washout of ≥84 days before first dose of study treatment.

data.description: Prior course of systemic corticosteroids (≥5 days) to modify immune AEs related to prior therapy requires washout of ≥14 days. data.name: Red blood cell transfusion

data.name: Treatment Compliance Threshold
data.description: Minimum compliance level required to maintain compliant status
data.text: A patient will be considered significantly noncompliant if judged to have intentionally or repeatedly taken more or less than prescribed. Compliance threshold is at least 80% unless otherwise specified in addendum Section 3.6.5

data.name: Re-screening Permission Requirement
data.description: Screen failures may only be re-screened after discussion with and permission from Lilly CRP/CRS or designee
data.text: Individuals who do not meet criteria for participation may be re-screened only after discussion with and permission from the Lilly CRP/CRS or designee. Screening laboratory tests may not be repeated more than twice to meet eligibility during the screening period

data.name: Continued Access Clinical Benefit Requirement
data.description: Patients may continue treatment during continued access period only if experiencing clinical benefit and no undue risks
data.text: Patients on addendum who are still on study treatment may continue to receive study treatment if they are experiencing clinical benefit and no undue risks

data.name: Inadvertent Enrollment Continuation Criteria
data.description: Criteria for allowing inadvertently enrolled patients to continue
data.text: If Lilly and investigator both agree it is medically appropriate to continue, investigator must obtain documented approval from Lilly CRP/CRS to allow inadvertently enrolled patient to continue with or without study treatment

data.name: Adaptive Randomization Rules

data.text: Some addenda may incorporate adaptive treatment randomization methodology, in which case the adaptation rules will be described in the addendum

data.text: The patient has had maximum dose reductions allowed per protocol and experiences an AE that would cause an additional dose reduction

data.text: The patient has radiographic progressive disease or significant symptomatic disease deterioration characterized as progression of disease, in the opinion of investigator, in the absence of radiographic evidence of PD

data.name: Unacceptable Toxicity

data.text: The patient experiences unacceptable toxicity (for example, a persistent moderate toxicity that is intolerable to the patient)

data.text: The patient becomes pregnant during the study

data.description: Discontinuation from study drug triggered when patient requires treatment with another demonstrated effective therapy
data.text: If the patient, for any reason, requires treatment with another therapeutic agent that has been demonstrated to be effective for treatment of the study indication, discontinuation from the study drug(s) occurs prior to introduction of the other agent

data.name: Long-Term Follow-Up Exclusion During Continued Access
data.description: Long-term follow-up does not apply during continued access period
data.text: Long-term follow-up during the study treatment period does not apply during the continued access period. Patients who are in long-term follow-up when the continued access period begins will be discontinued from long-term follow-up

data.name: Short-Term Follow-Up Completion During Continued Access
data.description: Patients in short-term follow-up when continued access begins continue until 30-day visit is completed
data.text: For patients who are in short-term follow-up during the study treatment period when the continued-access period begins, they will continue in short-term follow-up until the 30-day short-term follow-up visit is completed

data.name: Screen to Treatment Transition
data.text: Subject must meet all general and investigation-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria, including negative pregnancy test within 7 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 for females of childbearing potential

data.name: Treatment to Continued Access Transition
data.text: After final analysis of investigation-specific addendum and Lilly declaration that continued access period has begun, patients still on study treatment may continue if experiencing clinical benefit and no undue risks

data.name: Continued Access to Follow-Up Transition
data.text: Continued access follow-up begins when patient and investigator agree to discontinue study treatment and lasts approximately 30 (±7) days

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Disease Progression
data.text: Patient has radiographic progressive disease or significant symptomatic disease deterioration characterized as progression of disease in the opinion of investigator

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Unacceptable Toxicity
data.text: Patient experiences unacceptable toxicity (e.g., a persistent moderate toxicity that is intolerable to the patient)

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Maximum Dose Reductions Reached
data.text: Patient has had maximum dose reductions allowed per protocol and experiences an AE that would cause an additional dose reduction

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Noncompliance
data.text: Patient is noncompliant with study procedures and/or treatment; compliance threshold is at least 80% unless otherwise specified. Potential discontinuation will be discussed between investigator and Lilly CRP/CRS before final determination

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Competing Study Enrollment
data.text: Patient is enrolled in any other clinical study involving an investigational product or any other type of medical research judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Investigator Decision
data.text: Investigator/physician decides that the patient should be discontinued from the study or study drug(s)

data.name: Discontinuation from Study Treatment - Alternative Effective Therapy
data.text: Patient requires treatment with another therapeutic agent that has been demonstrated to be effective for treatment of the study indication; discontinuation from study drug occurs prior to introduction of the other agent

data.name: Dose Modification Due to AE
data.text: Dose modifications triggered by AEs must be reported to Lilly or designee via CRF/electronic data entry, clarifying circumstances leading to dose modification. Specific dose modification instructions defined in each addendum

data.name: Screen Failure to Alternative Investigation
data.text: Individuals who do not meet criteria for participation in an individual investigation may be considered for another investigation within the CAMPFIRE Master Protocol for which they are eligible

data.name: Discontinuation from Long-Term Follow-Up at Continued Access Start
data.text: Patients who are in long-term follow-up when the continued access period begins will be discontinued from long-term follow-up

data.name: Study Site Discontinuation
data.text: Study site participation may be discontinued if Lilly, the investigator, or the ERB/IRB of the study site judges it necessary for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and GCP

data.name: Full Study Discontinuation
data.text: The study will be discontinued if Lilly judges it necessary for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and GCP

data.name: Early Termination - Disease Progression
data.description: Patient discontinued due to radiographic progressive disease or significant symptomatic disease deterioration in the opinion of the investigator

data.name: Early Termination - Unacceptable Toxicity
data.description: Patient discontinued due to unacceptable toxicity such as persistent moderate toxicity intolerable to the patient

data.name: Early Termination - Maximum Dose Reductions
data.description: Patient discontinued after reaching maximum allowed dose reductions and experiencing an AE requiring further dose reduction

data.name: Early Termination - Noncompliance
data.description: Patient discontinued due to significant noncompliance with study procedures and/or treatment below 80% threshold, following discussion between investigator and Lilly CRP/CRS

data.name: Early Termination - Pregnancy
data.description: Patient discontinued due to pregnancy occurring during the study; pregnancy must be reported following the SAE process to collect data on outcome for both mother and fetus

data.name: Early Termination - Competing Study
data.description: Patient discontinued due to enrollment in another clinical study involving an investigational product judged not to be scientifically or medically compatible with this study

data.name: Early Termination - Investigator Decision
data.description: Patient discontinued based on investigator/physician decision

data.name: Early Termination - Patient/Guardian Decision
data.description: Patient discontinued at request of patient, parent, or legal guardian

data.name: Early Termination - Alternative Effective Therapy Required
data.description: Patient discontinued from study drug prior to introduction of another therapeutic agent demonstrated to be effective for the study indication

data.name: Study Completion - Investigation-Specific
data.description: Completion of all protocol-required visits as defined in the investigation-specific addendum, following final analysis as determined by Lilly

data.name: Continued Access Period End
data.description: Patient's continued access ends when a criterion for discontinuation is met (Section 8); continued access follow-up lasts approximately 30 (±7) days after patient and investigator agree to discontinue study treatment

data.name: Lost to Follow-Up
data.description: Patient considered lost to follow-up if repeatedly failing to return for scheduled visits and unable to be contacted by the study site despite diligent attempts by site personnel

data.name: Protocol Deviation - Inadvertent Enrollment
data.description: Patient who did not meet enrollment criteria and was inadvertently enrolled may be discontinued unless both Lilly CRP/CRS and investigator agree it is medically appropriate to continue and documented approval is obtained

data.name: Study Site Closure
data.description: Study site participation discontinued if Lilly, investigator, or ERB/IRB judges it necessary for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and GCP

data.name: Full Study Discontinuation by Sponsor
data.description: Entire study discontinued if Lilly judges it necessary for medical, safety, regulatory, or other reasons consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and GCP

data.name: Continued Access Eligibility Decision
data.description: Decision point after final analysis of investigation-specific addendum to determine if patients may continue in continued access period based on clinical benefit and absence of undue risks

data.name: Inadvertent Enrollment Continuation Decision
data.description: Decision point when inadvertent enrollment is identified; Lilly CRP/CRS and investigator must jointly determine if patient may continue in the study

data.name: Noncompliance Discontinuation Decision
data.description: Decision point when patient compliance falls below 80% threshold; potential discontinuation must be discussed between investigator and Lilly CRP/CRS before final determination

data.name: Screen Failure Re-screening Decision
data.description: Decision point for screen failures to determine eligibility for re-screening (requires Lilly CRP/CRS permission) or transfer to alternative investigation within CAMPFIRE

data.name: Long-Term Follow-Up Discontinuation at Continued Access
data.description: Decision point at start of continued access period to determine follow-up pathway: patients in short-term follow-up continue to 30-day visit; patients in long-term follow-up are discontinued from long-term follow-up

data.description: When patient is discontinued due to symptomatic deterioration, every effort should be made to document disease progression unless not medically appropriate
